title: GPU whale event: queue amplification, graceful eviction, and safety-net automation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: After a sudden high-volume tenant burst (a 'whale' of large concurrent multi-second streaming requests), hosted-api experienced GPU capacity exhaustion in one region. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, short-term mitigations that were deployed, and the longer-term safety-net and automation tasks required to prevent similar amplification events.
incident_summary: At 2025-02-11T03:14Z a single tenant issued a sequence of large batched streaming generation requests that overloaded the GPU pool. Automatic prefetching and admission heuristics requeued and amplified traffic, triggering autoscaler hysteresis and delaying scale-up. The result was multi-minute queue growth, elevated token latency, error rates for best-effort tenants, and customer-visible timeouts for some SLO-backed riders.
timeline: 2025-02-11T03:14Z - First sustained spike detected by pool QPS alarms (region us-west-2)
2025-02-11T03:16Z - Token latency > 95th increased from 220ms to 2.6s; some requests began timing out in the edge layer
2025-02-11T03:18Z - Autoscaler attempted to scale but prewarm hysteresis delayed full capacity by ~3 minutes
2025-02-11T03:20Z - Admission controller incorrectly scored prefetch jobs as high priority, allowing aggressive queueing
2025-02-11T03:25Z - Emergency tenant throttling applied for the suspected whale; build of quick eviction rule deployed
2025-02-11T03:36Z - Pool reached stable target capacity after manual priming and targeted eviction; error rates fell to normal over the next 6 minutes
root_cause: Compound failure: (1) an aggressive client workload (large batched streams) acted like a single-tenant whale, (2) prefetch/prefix caching heuristics allowed speculative work to occupy GPU slots, (3) admission scoring bug incorrectly boosted prefetch priority, and (4) autoscaler hysteresis + slow cold-start of GPU slots delayed effective scale-up.
impact: Hosted API customers in us-west-2 saw token latencies spike (P95 -> 2.6s), 12% increase in 5xx for a 22-minute window, and several high-revenue tenants reported timeouts. Internal monitoring alerted SRE; incident SLA targets were missed for P0 customers in that region.
immediate_mitigations_deployed: Applied temporary tenant throttles (rate cap) to suspected whale for 30 minutes
Rolled out emergency eviction rule to drop speculative prefetch jobs when queue depth > 80%
Manually primed additional GPU capacity via reserved warm pool (fast path) to shorten cold start
Updated edge timeouts to fail fast for best-effort routes to reduce queue amplification
action_items: ENG-562008: Implement per-tenant sustained-QPS detection and automated soft-throttle (owner: Priya Patel, estimate: 5)
ENG-562009: Limit speculative prefetch budget per pool; expose prefetch caps as runtime config (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 3)
ENG-562010: Fix admission scoring bug where prefetch jobs inherit high priority from origin keys (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2)
ENG-562011: Autoscaler tuning - reduce hysteresis window and add fast-priming path for short-duration bursts (owner: Infra Autoscale, estimate: 5)
ENG-562012: Implement emergency fast-priming runbook + automation to prewarm N GPUs in <60s (owner: Runtime team, estimate: 8)
ENG-562013: Add queue-depth based circuit-breaker that rejects best-effort requests before they hit GPUs (owner: Edge team, estimate: 3)
ENG-562014: Expand telemetry: per-tenant queued-token meters, per-request prefetch attribution, and prefetch-to-serving ratio dashboards (owner: Observability, estimate: 3)
ENG-562015: Run chaos tests and synthetic 'whale' workload experiments in staging monthly to validate protections (owner: Testing, estimate: 2)
ENG-562016: Post-incident customer outreach and credits checklist (owner: Customer Success, estimate: 1)
ENG-562017: Review and harden admission policy regression tests in the CI gate (owner: QA, estimate: 2)
ENG-562018: Add per-tenant emergency ejection policy for extreme unfairness (>95th DBL) with safety cooldown (owner: Scheduling, estimate: 4)
ENG-562019: Draft runbook for cross-region failover for critical tenants (owner: SRE, estimate: 3)
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant soft-throttle automatically engages for sustained high QPS with observable reduction in helper prefetch work
Speculative prefetch cannot occupy more than X% of active GPU slots and is throttled when queue depth high
Autoscaler fast-priming reduces time-to-effective-capacity by >60% in synthetic whale tests
Dashboards and alerts surface prefetch-driven queue amplification events within 90s of start
followups_and_owners: Schedule 1-week postmortem review with SRE/Runtime/Edge/Customer Success (owner: Aisha Khan)
Ship ENG-562008..ENG-562014 as a grouped rollout with staged canary in us-west-2 (owner: Marcus Lee)
Include incident summary in quarterly reliability report and share root cause learnings with customers (owner: Reliability PM)
notes: This incident is notable because queue amplification was dominated by speculative prefetch, not only by request volume. That suggests we need to treat speculative work as a first-class safety hazard.
Cross-team coordination during the incident worked well (Edge and Runtime pushed emergency patches), but we lacked a single automated play that could be triggered quickly.
Recommend adding an 'incident button' in Console SRE view to trigger emergency ejection and tenant throttle workflows in future incidents.
postmortem_status: Draft - awaiting engineering and SRE sign-off
closing_criteria: All P0 action items (ENG-562008..ENG-562014) implemented in runtime-1.22 and verified in staged chaos tests; runbook published; customer outreach complete
